items.title: OpenAI wants companies to trust it with sensitive work by promising not to look at their data
items.summary: OpenAI is testing a new feature called "Private Inference" that lets companies run queries on its most powerful models without OpenAI being able to access the data. items.title: Amazon and Meta are in talks to end the block on Meta's AI shopping agent Muse in Amazon's online store.
items.summary: Amazon and Meta are in talks to bring back Muse, Meta's AI shopping agent that Amazon kicked off its platform in September. The two sides are stuck on ad revenue and who gets to control search results. That matters because Amazon's ad business generates $68.6 billion a year, and Muse already commands 51 percent of all agentic shopping orders. items.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant
items.summary: Google Deepmind uses AI agents to run experiments on their own for upcoming Gemini models. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement. For oversight, Deepmind intentionally leaves the agents' internal chains of thought untrained so they can be reviewed. Kavukcuoglu measures AGI by everyday user trust rather than benchmarks. items.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools
items.summary: Anthropic studied nearly 300 AI deployments across 58 US companies with sobering results. Nearly one in five still delivers no business value, held back by heavy review workloads, internal bottlenecks, and employee resistance. The researchers say the biggest hurdles stem from outdated company structures. The article Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools appeared first on The Decoder

items.title: Back-to-back cyber incidents at US financial investigators and spy agencies follow a string of federal hacks and outages
items.summary: The US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network took systems offline as a precaution after unauthorized access. Hours earlier, reports emerged of a separate breach at the CIA, NGA, and ODNI, in which investigators suspect attackers used the AI defense tool Artex. items.title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
items.summary: MIT researchers have developed a method that lets AI climate models get by with a single training run instead of the usual six to eight. An algorithm generates deliberately unrealistic scenarios with extreme CO2 or methane swings that make the model more robust. items.title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows
items.summary: Anthropic now lets you install Claude Artifacts as desktop apps on Mac and Windows, and a free account is enough. You build one in chat without writing code, and it can add menu bar items, send notifications, and create transparent windows. items.title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents
items.summary: Two years after launch, Anthropic reports more than 700 million monthly downloads for its MCP interface standard. New features such as background tasks, follow-up questions for users, and file uploads are meant to let Claude work more independently. items.title: Novartis CEO says AI will shave four years off drug development, not cure all disease
items.summary: Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, who also sits on Anthropic's board, is pushing back on the cure-all promises from Anthropic CEO Amodei and DeepMind founder Hassabis. AI will speed up drug development, he says, but it won't beat cancer in a decade. The real value lies "somewhere in the middle."
